findings.reason: the author would pin the SELENE reader to the existing loader seam and state that its psi/boundary/axis reduce to the EquilibriumGeometry contract, keeping one firewalled read path.
findings.text: §7 says it "adds a SELENE reference loader and its firewall tier" to efit_referee but does not name the seam it must use: read_efit_geometry(loader=...) already accepts any reader returning an EquilibriumGeometry and is the single firewall-gated read path (evaluator_context / _gate_open), so a SELENE loader named without that contract risks a second read path that bypasses the gate

findings.reason: the author should extend the machine-map packaged registry as the shot→machine owner (or state why only the benchmark needs a bare-shot declaration), so the machine name has one source across §4 and §7.
findings.text: §7 puts per-shot machine identity in BenchShot.machine (spine_bench/shots.py) as "one owner", but MachineMap.machine plus load_packaged_machine_map / map_for_shot already own which machine a shot range belongs to, and §4's transform_machine_description selects a catalogue without a stated route from a bare shot to its machine

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new modules hide their machinery behind small interfaces (eddb_remote.py: RemoteEddbExtractor / SshTransport / BatchResult; eddb.py: fetch_channels / write_channel / is_cached; selene_deck.py: one converter entry point), and the remaining design extends the existing engines (StoreEngine.open already receives the selected map; the netCDF engine reads the static-over-map layout) rather than adding a parallel one.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 declares per-shot machine identity in spine_bench/shots.py (BenchShot.machine) while imas_ambix/data/machine_map.py already owns which machine a shot's range belongs to (MachineMap.machine, load_packaged_machine_map, map_for_shot), and the plan names no owner that maps a bare shot to a machine for the non-benchmark read path.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied figures public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each remaining section states what it retires or merges (§4 retires the read_geometry_table machine branch, §6 supplies cocos_convention the JT-60SA cohort and generalises measure_diiid_convention rather than adding a second scorer, §7 adds two record fields and retires nothing because no scalar reference comparison exists).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — every mechanism the plan cites was opened and matches its account (machine_map.load_packaged_machine_map / map_for_shot, signal_map.load_packaged_signal_map, description_reader.read_geometry_table, cocos_convention.score_convention, challenge/loader.load_shot, efit_referee.judge_geometry / GeometryVerdict, spine_bench/shots.resolve_shotset_version, gs/artifact_resolution PINNED_* / resolve_machine_description, gs/machine_identity.identity_for_shot), but §7's SELENE addition does not name the existing injectable reference-loader seam it must use.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §7's EQDB reader adds a genuinely different remote script (eqdbms / eqdbget) and reuses the transport owner (eddb_remote.SshTransport) rather than wrapping or forking RemoteEddbExtractor, which is EDDB-shaped (hard-coded REMOTE_SCRIPT, EDDB paths); the plan states the cache cannot be reused (record shape differs) so the record store is a declared sibling, not a wrapper.
